nahhas-irab:26-26.t: Al-Ḥasan read وهم ينهون عنه وينون عنه: he cast the vowel of the hamza onto the nūn and dropped the hamza.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
In Arabic it is permissible to say إذ أقفوا على النّار, like أُقِّتَتْ [al-Mursalāt: 11]. The people of Medina and al-Kisāʾī read يا لَيْتَنا نُرَدُّ وَلا نُكَذِّبَ بِآياتِ رَبِّنا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ with all of it in the nominative (rafʿ). Abū Jaʿfar said: This is also how it is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr, and it is transmitted from him as وَلا نُكَذِّبَ بِآياتِ رَبِّنا with assimilation (idghām). The Kufans, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read يا لَيْتَنا نُرَدُّ وَلا نُكَذِّبَ in the accusative (naṣb), and وَنَكُونَ likewise. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir read يا ليتنا نرد ولا نكذب in the nominative and وَنَكُونَ ] in the accusative. Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd read يا ليتنا نردّ ولا نكذّب بآيات ربّنا with the fāʾ and the accusative. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The first reading, in the nominative, is on the basis that it is cut off from what precedes it; this is the view of Sībawayh. It has also been said: it is conjoined (ʿaṭf). The assimilation is good. The accusative after the wāw is on the basis that it is the answer to the wish (jawāb al-tamannī), and likewise with the fāʾ. The nominative of the first verb in the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir is on the basis of its being cut off from what precedes it, or of conjunction, and «ونكون» is made the answer.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: بَلْ بَدا لَهُمْ ما كانُوا يُخْفُونَ مِنْ قَبْلُ: there are two views on its meaning. One is that it refers to the hypocrites, because the term "unbelief" includes them, so the pronoun refers back to part of what was mentioned; this is eloquent Arabic usage. The other view is that whenever the Prophet ﷺ admonished the unbelievers they were afraid, and they hid that fear so that the weak among them would not become aware of it; then that was made manifest on the Day of Resurrection. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read وَلَوْ رُدُّوا with a kasra on the rāʾ, because the original form is رددوا, and the kasra of the dāl was shifted onto the rāʾ, as one says قيل and بيع. But there is a difference between them, because in قيل the vowel was shifted only because it is a weak verb (muʿtall), and yāʾ and wāw are not governed like other letters, since they so frequently change.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: وَقالُوا إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا حَياتُنَا الدُّنْيا: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). وَما نَحْنُ: the noun of mā. نَحْنُ: the predicate. [Translator's note: so in the source; one would expect نحن to be the noun of mā and بمبعوثين its predicate.]

nahhas-irab:31-31.t:
قَدْ خَسِرَ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِلِقاءِ اللَّهِ, that is: they have lost their deeds and their reward. حَتَّى إِذا جاءَتْهُمُ السَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); according to Sībawayh it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl, as you say:
قتلته صبرا ("I killed him in confinement"), and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 131-
فلأيا بلأي ما حملنا وليدنا ... على ظهر محبوك ظماء مفاصله
(Only with great difficulty did we mount our lad on the back of a firm-bodied horse with lean joints.)
Sībawayh does not permit analogy to be drawn from it: one does not say جاء فلان سرعة. وَهُمْ يَحْمِلُونَ أَوْزارَهُمْ, that is, their sins; He made them, because of their heaviness, like a heavy load carried on the back. It has also been said: it means the punishments of sins, because punishment is called wizr. أَلا ساءَ ما يَزِرُونَ, that is, what they carry.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: وَمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا إِلَّا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); that is, those who desire the life of this world: it has no lasting outcome, so it is like amusement and play. وَلَلدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ: subject and predicate. Ibn ʿĀmir read ولدار الآخرة, lightened and in the genitive. And the abode of the Hereafter is better because it endures. لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ, that is, who guard against disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ that the matter is so, and so renounce this world?

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: قَدْ نَعْلَمُ إِنَّهُ لَيَحْزُنُكَ الَّذِي يَقُولُونَ: «إنّ» takes a kasra because of the entry of the lām. فَإِنَّهُمْ لا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ: we have already discussed it. It is reported that Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: يكذبونك and يكذّبونك have one meaning. He said: لا يكذبونك may mean "they do not find you bringing falsehood", as you say أبخلت الرجل ("I found the man stingy"). Someone else said: the meaning of لا يكذّبونك is "they do not give you the lie with any proof or demonstration", and this is indicated by وَلكِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
وَلَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ: on the feminine of the group. رُسُلٌ: the noun of the verb whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent); if you wish you may drop the ḍamma and say رسل, because the ḍamma is heavy. فَصَبَرُوا عَلى ما كُذِّبُوا, that is: so be patient as they were patient.
وَأُوذُوا حَتَّى أَتاهُمْ نَصْرُنا, that is: so what you have been promised will come to you. وَلا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِماتِ اللَّهِ explains this; that is, what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has promised, no one is able to avert.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: وَإِنْ كانَ: a condition. كَبُرَ: a past verb, and it is the khabar (predicate) of kāna. فَإِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقاً فِي الْأَرْضِ: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). أَوْ سُلَّماً فِي السَّماءِ: conjoined to it, that is, a means of reaching the sky. This is a figurative representation, because the ladder by which one climbs is a means to the place. What al-Farrāʾ reported about the feminine gender of سلّم is not known. فَتَأْتِيَهُمْ بِآيَةٍ: conjoined. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded the Prophet ﷺ not to grieve intensely over them since they would not believe, just as he was not able to do this. فَلا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْجاهِلِينَ: of those whose grief became intense and who lamented until it drove them to extreme despair and to what is not permitted.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: إِنَّما يَسْتَجِيبُ الَّذِينَ يَسْمَعُونَ, that is, they listen with the listening of attention, understanding and desire for the truth. وَالْمَوْتى يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ: these are the unbelievers, and they are like the dead in that they neither accept nor give ear to any proof.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: وَقالُوا لَوْلا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ: this was obstinacy on their part after the proofs had become manifest and the argument had been established by the Qur'an, whose like they were unable to produce even a single sura of, because of the description and knowledge of the unseen it contains. وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends down only those signs in which there is benefit for His servants.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: وَما مِنْ دَابَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا طائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَناحَيْهِ: conjoined to the wording (ʿaṭf ʿalā al-lafẓ). Al-Ḥasan and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Isḥāq read وَلا طائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَناحَيْهِ, making it conjoined to the position (ʿalā al-mawḍiʿ), the implied form being: وما دابة ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه. [Translator's note: the vowelling of this variant as printed is identical to the main reading; the variant intended is presumably the nominative طائرٌ.] إِلَّا أُمَمٌ أَمْثالُكُمْ, that is, they are communities like you in that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created them, guaranteed their provision and dealt justly with them, so you should not wrong them nor go beyond what you have been commanded concerning them. دابّة applies to everything that creeps. ما فَرَّطْنا فِي الْكِتابِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ, that is, We have left out nothing of the matter of religion without having pointed to it in the Qur'an, either by a clear, explained indication or by a general one, such as وَما آتاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَما نَهاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَانْتَهُوا [al-Ḥashr: 7]. ثُمَّ إِلى رَبِّهِمْ يُحْشَرُونَ: by this He indicated that the beasts will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا صُمٌّ وَبُكْمٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). مَنْ يَشَأِ اللَّهُ يُضْلِلْهُ: condition and requital (sharṭ wa-mujāzāh), and likewise وَمَنْ يَشَأْ يَجْعَلْهُ عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
قُلْ أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ with both hamzas fully pronounced is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza. Nāfiʿ read it lightening the hamzas: he casts the vowel of the first onto what precedes it and pronounces the second "between and between" (bayna bayna). Abū ʿUbayd reported from him that he drops the hamza and substitutes an alif for it; according to the philologists this is an error attributed to him, because the yāʾ is quiescent and the alif is quiescent, and two quiescent letters do not come together. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Kisāʾī read قل أريتكم, dropping the second hamza; this is far-fetched in Arabic and is permissible only in poetry. The Arabs say: أريتك زيدا ما شأنه ("Tell me about Zayd, what is his state?"). Al-Farrāʾ said: the kāf has the form of an accusative but the meaning of a nominative, as one says دونك زيدا, that is, "take him". Abū Isḥāq said: this is impossible; rather the kāf has no grammatical position and is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, as one says ذاك. On this basis the Arabs say in the dual أريتكما زيدا ما شأنه, in the plural أريتكم زيدا, and to a woman أريتك زيدا ما شأنه: they leave the tāʾ singular and put the marker on the kāf. If the kāf is in the position of the accusative they say in the dual:
أريتما كما عالمين بفلان, in the plural أريتموكم عالمين بفلان, for a group of women أريتكنّ عالمات بفلان, and for a single woman أريتك عالمة بزيد. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَيَطْغى أَنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنى [al-ʿAlaq: 6–7], and it is of exactly this kind.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: إِيَّاهُ: accusative governed by تدعون. فَيَكْشِفُ ما تَدْعُونَ إِلَيْهِ: an imperfect (future) verb. وَتَنْسَوْنَ: "and you abandon", like وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنا إِلى آدَمَ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَنَسِيَ [Ṭā Hā: 115]. It may also mean: you abandon, and so you are like those who forget. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj read [Translator's note: the source names no reading here; the text appears to be defective]. مَنْ إِلهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ انْظُرْ with a ḍamma on the hāʾ according to the original form, because the hāʾ is originally with ḍamma, as you say جئت معه. We have already discussed the use of the singular hāʾ.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: Al-Kisāʾī said: one says بغتهم الأمر يبغتهم بغتا وبغتة when it comes upon them suddenly. Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash read الْعَذابُ بِما with assimilation, and so it is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr with assimilation. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read بِما كانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ with a kasra on the sīn, and it is a well-known dialect form.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: وَلا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ: jussive (majzūm) by the prohibition; the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the ḍamma, and the dāl takes a kasra because two quiescent letters meet. يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَداةِ: غداة is indefinite and was made definite with alif and lām; it is written with a wāw just as الصلاة is written with a wāw. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir and Mālik ibn Dīnār read بِالْغَداةِ [Translator's note: the variant intended is بالغُدوة, which the following explanation discusses; the printed text repeats the main reading]. The rule for غدوة is that it is definite, but it may be made indefinite just as proper nouns are made indefinite, and when it is made indefinite alif and lām enter it to make it definite. عشيّ and عشيّة are indefinite only. ما عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسابِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ: the first (من) is partitive and the second is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and likewise وَما مِنْ حِسابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ. فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ: the answer to the negation. فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ: the answer to the prohibition.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: The lām of purpose (lām kay). This is one of the difficult points. It is asked: how were they tried so that they would say this, since if it was a denial it is unbelief on their part? There are two answers to this. One is that the meaning is: We tried the rich by means of the poor, in that their standing with the Prophet ﷺ was one and the same, so that they would say by way of question, not by way of denial, أَهؤُلاءِ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ بَيْنِنا. The other answer is that when they were tried by this, and its outcome led to their saying this by way of denial, it became like the saying of Him, Majestic and Mighty: فَالْتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَناً [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8].

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: فَقُلْ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and according to Sībawayh it carries the meaning of the accusative; that is why it begins with an indefinite noun. كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ, that is, He made it binding; the servants were addressed in terms of what they know, namely that whoever writes something down has made it binding on himself. It has also been said: He wrote that in the Preserved Tablet. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have already mentioned the reading of those who read (أنّه) (فأنه) with a fatḥa on both, the reading of those who put a kasra on both, and the reading of those who put a fatḥa on the first and a kasra on the second. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj read with a kasra on the first and a fatḥa on the second; so Ibn Saʿdān transmitted from him. Whoever gives both a fatḥa makes the first a badal (substitute) for الرحمة, or takes it as having an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "it is such-and-such"; and the second, according to Sībawayh, is a repetition ], as Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: لا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِما أَتَوْا وَيُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يُحْمَدُوا بِما لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ بِمَفازَةٍ مِنَ الْعَذابِ [Āl ʿImrān: 188], and He, Majestic and Mighty, said إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هادُوا and then said afterwards إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ [al-Ḥajj: 17]. Al-Akhfash and Abū Ḥātim said: the second «أنّ» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, that is, "then forgiveness is his". This is wrong according to Sībawayh, for Sībawayh does not allow a sentence to begin with أنّ. But some grammarians have said the second «أنّ» may be in the position of the nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "then what is his is that Allah is Forgiving, Merciful". Whoever puts a kasra on both makes the first the beginning of a new sentence and takes كتب in the sense of "said", and puts a kasra on the second because it comes after the fāʾ in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). Whoever puts a kasra on the first and a fatḥa on the second treats the first as we said and puts a fatḥa on the second on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ; Abū Ḥātim rejected this reading, as it had not reached him. Whoever puts a fatḥa on the first and a kasra on the second treats the first as we mentioned for the one who gives both a fatḥa, and puts a kasra on the second as is required for it after the fāʾ; this reading is clear in Arabic.

nahhas-irab:55-56.t: وَكَذلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآياتِ وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ: it is said: this lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to a verb, so where is the verb to which it is attached? The Kufans say: the implied form is وكذلك نفصّل الآيات لنبيّن لكم ولتستبين سبيل المجرمين. Abū Jaʿfar said: none of this ellipsis is needed; the implied form is: وكذلك نفصّل الآيات، ولتستبين سبيل المجرمين فصّلناها. سبيل is treated as both masculine and feminine, the feminine being more common. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read قَدْ ضَلَلْتُ إِذاً with a kasra on the lām, and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: ضللت is the dialect of Tamīm.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: قُلْ إِنِّي عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّي وَكَذَّبْتُمْ بِهِ: the pronoun refers back to البيّنة, and it is masculine because البيان and البيّنة are one and the same. It has also been said: the implied form is "and you denied what I have brought". Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already discussed يقضي الحقّ and يَقُصُّ الْحَقَّ.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: قُلْ لَوْ أَنَّ عِنْدِي ما تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِهِ, that is, of the punishment. لَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ, that is, it would have been cut off, to the end of the verse.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: وَعِنْدَهُ مَفاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ, which opens the knowledge of the unseen when He, Majestic and Mighty, wishes to inform a prophet or someone else of it. مفاتح is the plural of مفتح; this is the eloquent usage, and one also says مفتاح, the plural being مفاتيح. Al-Ḥasan and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Isḥāq read ولا رطب لا يابس إلّا في كتاب مّبين, conjoined to the meaning. [Translator's note: so in the source, "لا يابس" without wāw; the variant intended is presumably the nominative ولا رطبٌ ولا يابسٌ.] It is also permissible to take وَلا حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُماتِ الْأَرْضِ as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ مُبِينٍ, that is, Allah wrote it down so that the angels would take heed of it.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); that is, He takes the full count of you. بِاللَّيْلِ and في الليل are the same. Abū Rajāʾ and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read ثم يبعثكم فيه ليقضي أجلا مسمّى.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: حَتَّى إِذا جاءَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ: this is the preference of al-Khalīl, and it is the reading of Nāfiʿ, lightening the second hamza. It is also permissible to lighten both and to drop one of them. تَوَفَّتْهُ رُسُلُنا: on the feminine of the group, as He said: فَلَمَّا جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ [Ghāfir: 83]. Ḥamza read توفّاه رسلنا, treating the plural as masculine, and al-Aʿmash read يتوفّاه رسلنا, with an added yāʾ at its beginning and the masculine.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: ثُمَّ رُدُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلاهُمُ الْحَقِّ: as a naʿt (adjective). Al-Ḥasan read الحقّ in the accusative, which may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) or in the sense of "I mean" (aʿnī). The meaning of مولاهم الحقّ is that He is their Creator, their Provider, the One who benefits them and harms them, and none is so but Allah, Majestic and Mighty. أَلا لَهُ, that is: know and say that His alone is the judgement.

nahhas-irab:63-63.t: تَدْعُونَهُ تَضَرُّعاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), the meaning being "possessed of humility". Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh transmitted from ʿĀṣim وَخُفْيَةً with a kasra on the khāʾ, and it is transmitted from al-Aʿmash وخيفة, with the yāʾ before the fāʾ; this is a far-fetched meaning, because the meaning of تضرعا is that they show abasement openly, and خفية that they conceal the like of that. The Kufans read لَئِنْ أَنْجانا, but the coherence of the passage favours the tāʾ, as the people of Medina and the people of Syria read it.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t:
أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ شِيَعاً. It is transmitted from Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Madanī أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ»
with a ḍamma on the yāʾ, that is, He will cover you with punishment and envelop you in it; this is from اللُّبس with a ḍamma on the lām, while the first is from اللَّبس with a fatḥa. [Translator's note: so in the source.] It is a difficult passage, and the i'rab clarifies it. It has been said: the implied form is "or He will confuse your affair for you", one of the two objects and the preposition having been omitted, as Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَإِذا كالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَزَنُوهُمْ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 3]. This confusion consists in some of them being let loose to fight others, or in His showing them a sign at which they split up, so that they are seen as factions. شِيَعاً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) or as a maṣdar (verbal noun). It has also been said: the meaning of يلبسكم شيعا is that He strengthens your enemy until it mingles with you, and when it mingles with you it has clothed you in divisions. وَيُذِيقَ بَعْضَكُمْ بَأْسَ بَعْضٍ: by war.

nahhas-irab:66-67.t:
قُلْ لَسْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِوَكِيلٍ: I have not been commanded to guard you against denial and unbelief.
It is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās: لِكُلِّ نَبَإٍ مُسْتَقَرٌّ, that is, every report has a reality.

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: وَإِذا رَأَيْتَ الَّذِينَ يَخُوضُونَ فِي آياتِنا: the implied form is: "and when you see those who plunge into Our signs with denial, rejection and mockery". فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ, disapproving of them. حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ وَإِمَّا يُنْسِيَنَّكَ الشَّيْطانُ فَلا تَقْعُدْ بَعْدَ الذِّكْرى مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ: thus Allah, Majestic and Mighty, disciplined His Prophet ﷺ, because he used to sit with a group of the polytheists, admonishing them and calling them, and they would mock the Qur'an; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to turn away from it with the turning away of one who disapproves, and not to give it attention. In this there is a refutation, in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of those who claim that the imams, who are proofs, and their followers may mix with the transgressors and approve their opinions out of taqiyya (dissimulation). ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir read وَإِمَّا يُنْسِيَنَّكَ الشَّيْطانُ in the intensive form. [Translator's note: the intended reading is يُنَسِّيَنَّكَ with a doubled sīn; the printed vowelling is that of the main reading.]

nahhas-irab:69-69.t:
وَلكِنْ ذِكْرى: in the position of the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). It may also be in the position of the nominative, meaning «ولكن الذي يفعلونه ذكرى» ("but what they do is a reminder"), that is, "but upon them is a reminder". Al-Kisāʾī said:
the meaning is "but this is a reminder".

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: وَذَكِّرْ بِهِ أَنْ تُبْسَلَ: in the position of the accusative, that is, "for fear (karāhata) that it be given up to destruction". بِما كانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ: in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كانوا.

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: قُلْ أَنَدْعُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَنْفَعُنا وَلا يَضُرُّنا وَنُرَدُّ عَلى أَعْقابِنا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدانَا اللَّهُ كَالَّذِي اسْتَهْوَتْهُ الشَّياطِينُ فِي الْأَرْضِ حَيْرانَ لَهُ أَصْحابٌ يَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى الْهُدَى ائْتِنا قُلْ إِنَّ هُدَى اللَّهِ هُوَ الْهُدى وَأُمِرْنا لِنُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ (71) قُلْ أَنَدْعُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَنْفَعُنا, that is, what does not benefit us if we call upon it. وَلا يَضُرُّنا if we abandon it. وَنُرَدُّ عَلى أَعْقابِنا, that is, we return to error after guidance. The singular of أعقاب is عقب; it is feminine and its diminutive is عقيبة. كَالَّذِي: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as the naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar. اسْتَهْوَتْهُ الشَّياطِينُ: on the feminine of the group. Ḥamza read استهواه الشياطين, treating the plural as masculine. It is transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd استهواه الشيطان, and from al-Ḥasan استهوته الشياطون ]; Maḥbūb transmitted it from ʿAmr from al-Ḥasan, and it is a solecism (laḥn). حَيْرانَ: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is a diptote because its feminine is حيرى. لَهُ أَصْحابٌ يَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى الْهُدَى ائْتِنا: when beginning with it, ائتنا [Translator's note: i.e. pronounced ītinā]; the original form has two hamzas, one of which was changed into a yāʾ so that they would not come together. وَأُمِرْنا لِنُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ: the lām of purpose (lām kay). Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān say: it is the lām of the genitive; all lāms are three: the lām of the genitive, the lām of command and the lām of emphasis, and nothing falls outside them.

nahhas-irab:72-73.t:
وَأَنْ أَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ: there are three views on it. Al-Farrāʾ's position is that the meaning is "and we were commanded that we submit and that: establish prayer". The second answer is that the meaning is "and with: establish the prayer". The third is that it is conjoined to the meaning, that is, they call him to guidance and call him to: establish prayer, because the meaning of «ائتنا» is "that: come to us".
وَهُوَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ. وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ: there are three answers concerning it: it may be conjoined to the hāʾ in وَاتَّقُوهُ; the second is that it is conjoined to السموات; and the third is that it is in the sense of "remember". كُنْ فَيَكُونُ: there are three answers concerning it. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is said that it concerns the Trumpet specifically: «ويوم يقول للصور كن فيكون» ("and the day He says to the Trumpet 'Be', and it is"). The second answer is that the meaning is: then everything He willed comes to be, of people's death and their life. On these two answers قَوْلُهُ الْحَقُّ is mubtadaʾ and khabar. The third answer is that قوله is nominative as the subject of يكون and الحقّ is its naʿt (adjective). يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ: there are three answers concerning it: it may be a badal (substitute) for يوم; the second answer is that the implied form is "His word is the truth on the day the Trumpet is blown"; and the third answer is that the implied form is "and His is the dominion on the day the Trumpet is blown". عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ: there are three answers concerning it: it may be a naʿt of الذي, that is, "and He it is who created the heavens, the Knower of the unseen"; it may be on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ. Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ [Translator's note: the variant intended is the genitive عالمِ; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading], which may be a badal for the hāʾ in (له). The third answer for the nominative is that it is construed according to the meaning, that is, the Knower of the unseen blows into it, because since the blowing into it is by the command of Allah it is attributed to Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 132-
ليبك يزيد ضارع لخصومة ... وأشعث ممّن طوّحته الطّوائح
(Let Yazīd be wept for — by one humbled in a dispute, and by a dishevelled man of those whom calamities have cast far away.)

nahhas-irab:74-74.t:
وَإِذْ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ آزَرَ: the scholars have discussed this. Al-Ḥasan said: his father's name was Āzar. It has been said that he had two names, Āzar and Tāraḥ. Al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulaymān transmitted from his father, who said: it has reached me that it means "crooked"; he said: and it is the harshest word Ibrāhīm ﷺ said to his father. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the meaning of آزر is "old man".
Abū Jaʿfar said: this may be derived from الأزر, which is the back; it is a diptote because it is on the pattern afʿal, and it would be a badal (substitute), as one says رجل أجوف, that is, "great of belly"; likewise آزر would be "great of back, crooked in it". It is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read وإذ قال إبراهيم لأبيه أازرا with two hamzas, the first with fatḥa and the second with kasra; this is the transmission of Abū Ḥātim, and he did not explain its meaning. It may be derived from الأزر, the back, its meaning being strength, and it would be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); it may also be in the sense of وزر, as one says وسادة and إسادة. In a transmission other than Abū Ḥātim's it is with two hamzas both with fatḥa, and in both transmissions تَتَّخِذُ without an alif. أَصْناماً آلِهَةً: two objects, and it carries the sense of disapproval. إِنِّي أَراكَ وَقَوْمَكَ: conjoined to the kāf.

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: Abū al-Sammāl al-ʿAdawī read وَكَذلِكَ نُرِي إِبْراهِيمَ مَلَكُوتَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ with a sukūn on the lām. According to Sībawayh dropping the fatḥa is not permissible because of its lightness; perhaps it is a dialect form. وَلِيَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُوقِنِينَ, that is: and so that he would be one of those with certainty, We showed him.

nahhas-irab:76-76.t: فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ رَأى كَوْكَباً: an object. قالَ هذا رَبِّي: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Among the best things said about this is what is authentically reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said concerning the words of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, نُورٌ عَلى نُورٍ [al-Nūr: 35]: "Thus is the heart of the believer: it knows Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and reasons its way to Him with its heart, and when it knows Him it increases in light upon light." Likewise Ibrāhīm ﷺ knew Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with his heart and reasoned his way to Him by His signs, and so knew that he had a Lord and Creator; and when Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made Himself known to him, his knowledge increased, and he said: أَتُحاجُّونِّي فِي اللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدانِ [al-Anʿām: 80].

nahhas-irab:78-78.t:
فَلَمَّا رَأَى الشَّمْسَ بازِغَةً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because this is seeing with the eye. قالَ هذا رَبِّي: al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash said: that is, he said "this rising one is my Lord". Others said: that is, "this light". Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: that is, "this figure", as al-Aʿshā said: [al-Sarīʿ] 133-
قامت تبكّيه على قبره ... من لي من بعدك يا عامر
تركتني في الدّار ذا غربة ... قد ذلّ من ليس له ناصر
(She stood weeping for him at his grave: "Who is there for me after you, O ʿĀmir? You have left me in the abode a stranger; humbled is he who has no helper.")

nahhas-irab:79-79.t: That is: I have directed my worship and my affirmation of oneness to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, alone. وَما أَنَا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ: the noun of «ما» and its predicate. When you pause you say أنا, adding the alif to show the vowel; and among the Arabs are those who say «انه».

nahhas-irab:80-80.t:
وَحاجَّهُ قَوْمُهُ قالَ أَتُحاجُّونِّي: Nāfiʿ read أتحاجّوني with a single, light nūn. It is reported that Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: it is a solecism (laḥn). Sībawayh permitted it and said: they found the doubling heavy; and he recited: [al-Wāfir] 134-
تراه كالثّغام يعلّ مسكا ... يسوء الفاليات إذا فليني
(You see it [i.e. grey hair] like the white thughām plant, steeped again and again in musk; it vexes the women who search it for lice when they search me.)
Abū ʿUbayda said: those who disliked the doubled form disliked it only because of the combination of two quiescent letters, namely the wāw and the nūn, so they dropped it. Abū Jaʿfar said: the right view on this is the view of Sībawayh; the combination of two quiescent letters is not objectionable when the first is a letter of prolongation and softness and the second is assimilated. وَقَدْ هَدانِ, with the yāʾ dropped because the kasra indicates it and the nūn compensates for it when you drop it; retaining it is good. وَلا أَخافُ ما تُشْرِكُونَ بِهِ, that is, because it neither benefits nor harms; ما is in the position of the accusative. إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ رَبِّي شَيْئاً: in the position of the accusative as an exception not of the same kind as the first (istithnāʾ laysa min al-awwal). وَسِعَ رَبِّي كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْماً: specification (bayān).

nahhas-irab:81-81.t: وَكَيْفَ أَخافُ ما أَشْرَكْتُمْ: an object, and likewise وَلا تَخافُونَ أَنَّكُمْ أَشْرَكْتُمْ بِاللَّهِ ما لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ عَلَيْكُمْ سُلْطاناً, that is, an argument. فَأَيُّ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ أَحَقُّ بِالْأَمْنِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ, that is: if you know, then whoever fears the One who benefits and harms is more entitled to security than you.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَلَمْ يَلْبِسُوا إِيمانَهُمْ بِظُلْمٍ: mubtadaʾ (subject). أُولئِكَ: a second mubtadaʾ. لَهُمُ الْأَمْنُ: its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of the first. وَهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ: mubtadaʾ and khabar.

nahhas-irab:83-83.t: Likewise وَتِلْكَ حُجَّتُنا. The reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and of Abū ʿAmr is نَرْفَعُ دَرَجاتٍ مَنْ نَشاءُ with the genitive construct (iḍāfa); the people of Kufa read نَرْفَعُ دَرَجاتٍ مَنْ نَشاءُ, the implied form being "and We raise whom We will to degrees", after which «إلى» was omitted. [Translator's note: the two readings are printed identically; the first intended is دَرَجاتِ مَن (construct), the second دَرَجاتٍ مَن (with tanwīn).]

nahhas-irab:84-84.t: وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ إِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ: two foreign names that are diptotes when definite and triptotes when indefinite. If you derive إسحاق from أسحقه الله ("Allah crushed him"), it is a triptote; likewise يعقوب, if it is a transferred (Arabic) name, is a triptote in every case; the male of the partridge is called يعقوب. كُلًّا: accusative governed by هدينا. وَنُوحاً: accusative governed by the second هدينا. وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِهِ داوُدَ وَسُلَيْمانَ: al-Farrāʾ said it is conjoined to نوح, and al-Akhfash said it is conjoined to إسحاق, and likewise وَأَيُّوبَ and what follows it. داود is a diptote because it is a foreign name, and every name on the pattern fāʿūl to which alif and lām are not well suited is a diptote. سليمان is a foreign name; it may also be derived from السلامة, and it is a diptote because it has an added alif and nūn. أيوب is a foreign name, and likewise يوسف. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read وَيُوسُفَ with a kasra on the sīn. Abū Zayd said: the Arabs say يؤسف with a hamza and a kasra on the sīn, and with a fatḥa on it, يؤسف, with hamza. موسى is a foreign name; as for موسى meaning the iron razor, if you name a man with it, it is a diptote because it is feminine. عيسى is a foreign name; if you take it as derived it is a diptote because at its end there is an alif resembling the alif of the feminine; its derivation is from عاسه يعوسه, the wāw having changed into a yāʾ because of the kasra before it. It may also be derived from العيس, which is the semen of the stallion.

nahhas-irab:85-85.t: وَزَكَرِيَّا: a foreign name; it may also be Arabic, with an alif of the feminine, and it is a diptote both when definite and when indefinite. وَيَحْيى: a diptote because it is originally from a verb, and it is written with a yāʾ to distinguish the noun from the verb. وَإِلْياسَ: foreign. Al-Aʿraj, al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read وَإِلْياسَ with a connecting alif (waṣl). Al-Farrāʾ said: in all of this the nominative is permissible, as you say: أخذت صدقاتهم لكلّ مائة شاة شاة وشاة ("I took their alms: for every hundred sheep, a sheep and a sheep").

nahhas-irab:86-86.t:
وَإِسْماعِيلَ: foreign. The people of the two Sanctuaries, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim read وَالْيَسَعَ with a light lām; the Kufans except ʿĀṣim read واللّيسع ], and so al-Kisāʾī read it, and he rejected the reading of those who read «واليسع», saying: because one does not say اليفعل, like اليحيى. This rejection is not binding, for the Arabs say:
اليعمل and اليحمد, and if you made يحيى indefinite you would say اليحيى. Abū Ḥātim rejected the reading of those who read (الّيسع) and said: ليسع is not found. Abū Jaʿfar said: this rejection is not binding; حيدر and زينب occur in the speech of the Arabs. The truth in this is that it is a foreign name, and foreign names are not taken by analogy but are transmitted by hearing, and the Arabs often alter them, so it is not objectionable for a name to come in two forms. وَيُونُسَ: foreign; and if you say يونس or يونس you do not make it a triptote, because it is originally from a verb. [Translator's note: the two alternative vowellings, presumably يونِس and يونَس, are not marked in the source.] وَلُوطاً: foreign, [a triptote] because of its lightness.

nahhas-irab:87-87.t: وَاجْتَبَيْناهُمْ, that is, We chose them; derived from جبيت الماء في الحوض, that is, "I gathered the water in the trough".

nahhas-irab:89-89.t: أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ وَالْحُكْمَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). فَإِنْ يَكْفُرْ بِها هؤُلاءِ: a condition, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَقَدْ وَكَّلْنا بِها قَوْماً, that is, a people to believe in it. لَيْسُوا بِها بِكافِرِينَ: the second bāʾ is for emphasis.

nahhas-irab:90-90.t: أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). فَبِهُداهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ: there are two views on it. One is that the meaning is "be patient as they were patient"; the other is that it is authentically reported that the Prophet ﷺ liked to follow the People of the Book in what he had not been forbidden and what had not been abrogated. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir read فَبِهُداهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ قُلْ لا أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً [Translator's note: the variant intended is اقتدهِ (or اقتدهي) with the hāʾ vowelled in continuous reading; the printed vowelling does not show it]; this is a solecism (laḥn), because the hāʾ is to show the vowel in pausing and is not a pronominal hāʾ, and it is not followed by a wāw or a yāʾ either. Nor is فَبِهُداهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ قُلْ لا أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً permissible. Whoever avoids solecism and follows the written text (al-sawād) reads فَبِهُداهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ, then pauses, then قُلْ لا أَسْئَلُكُمْ, and does not join them, because if he joined with the hāʾ it would be a solecism, and if he dropped it he would contradict the written text.

nahhas-irab:91-91.t:
وَما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ: a maṣdar (verbal noun). Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned that it has been said the meaning is "they did not magnify Allah as He truly deserves to be magnified"; this comes from their saying لفلان قدر ("so-and-so has standing"). The explanation of this is that when they said ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلى بَشَرٍ مِنْ شَيْءٍ, they ascribed to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, that He does not establish the proof against His servants nor command them what is good for them, so they did not magnify Him as He deserves nor know Him as He deserves to be known. It has also been said that the meaning is:
"they did not value the blessings of Allah as they deserve to be valued". Abū Ḥaywa read وَما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ with a fatḥa on the dāl, and it is a dialect form. [Translator's note: the variant intended is قَدَرِه; the printed vowelling does not show it.] تَجْعَلُونَهُ قَراطِيسَ, that is, in sheets, like وَاخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ [al-Aʿrāf: 155].

nahhas-irab:92-92.t: وَهذا كِتابٌ أَنْزَلْناهُ مُبارَكٌ: a naʿt (adjective); outside the Qur'an it would be permissible to put it in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise مُصَدِّقُ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ. وَلِتُنْذِرَ أُمَّ الْقُرى, that is, We sent it down for this.

nahhas-irab:94-94.t:
وَمَنْ قالَ: in the position of the genitive, that is, "and who is more unjust than one who says": سَأُنْزِلُ مِثْلَ ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ. وَلَوْ تَرى إِذِ الظَّالِمُونَ فِي غَمَراتِ الْمَوْتِ: the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, that is, "you would see a great punishment". وَالْمَلائِكَةُ باسِطُوا أَيْدِيهِمْ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the original form is باسطون أيديهم, saying أَخْرِجُوا أَنْفُسَكُمُ — [the word "saying"] being omitted; that is, "bring your souls out of the punishment", that is, rescue them. الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذابَ الْهُونِ, that is, the punishment of humiliation.
بِما كُنْتُمْ تَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ, that is, you claim a partner with Him and say: He did not send Muḥammad ﷺ.
وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونا فُرادى كَما خَلَقْناكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَتَرَكْتُمْ ما خَوَّلْناكُمْ وَراءَ ظُهُورِكُمْ وَما نَرى مَعَكُمْ شُفَعاءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّهُمْ فِيكُمْ شُرَكاءُ لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ وَضَلَّ عَنْكُمْ ما كُنْتُمْ تَزْعُمُونَ (94) وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونا فُرادى: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is a diptote because it contains an alif of the feminine. Abū Ḥaywa read فرادا with tanwīn. Hārūn said: the dialect of Tamīm is فرادا with tanwīn, and these people say,
in the position of the nominative, فراد. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā reported فراد without tanwīn, like ثلاث and رباع. Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is: you have come to Us alone, with no helper with you from among those who used to accompany you in error.
كَما خَلَقْناكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ: there are three views on it: it may mean alone, as they were created; it may mean naked; and it may mean "as We created you, We have brought you back". وَما نَرى مَعَكُمْ شُفَعاءَكُمُ, that is, those whom you worshipped and made partners in your wealth. لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ: Abū ʿAmr said: that is, your bond; and بَيْنَكُمْ as an adverb (ẓarf). [Translator's note: the two readings meant are بينُكم (nominative, "your bond") and بينَكم (adverbial); the printed vowelling does not distinguish them.]

nahhas-irab:95-95.t: إِنَّ اللَّهَ فالِقُ الْحَبِّ وَالنَّوى, that is, He splits the dead date-stone and brings forth from it green leaves, and likewise the grain; and He brings forth from the green leaves a dead stone and grain. This is the meaning of يُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَمُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتِ مِنَ الْحَيِّ. It is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās: He brings forth the living human from the dead sperm-drop, and the sperm-drop from the living human. ذلِكُمُ اللَّهُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ: so from where are you turned away from the truth, despite what you see of the power of Allah, Majestic and Mighty?

nahhas-irab:96-96.t:
فالِقُ الْإِصْباحِ: a naʿt (adjective); it is definite, and according to none of the grammarians may it take tanwīn, except according to al-Kisāʾī. The meaning of فالق الإصباح is the One who created for it a cleaving, namely the dawn. The dawn is called فلق الصّبح and فرقه. Al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read فالِقُ الْإِصْباحِ with a fatḥa on the hamza [Translator's note: i.e. الأصباح; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading], and it is the plural of صبح. Al-Aʿmash transmitted from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī that he read فلق الإصباح on the pattern faʿala, with the hamza with kasra and the ḥāʾ accusative. Al-Ḥasan, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read وَجَعَلَ اللَّيْلَ سَكَناً, that is, He made it suitable for resting in; the people of Medina read وجاعل الليل سكنا.
وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ حُسْباناً: الشمس and القمر are accusative, conjoined to the meaning, that is, "and He made". The genitive is far-fetched because the governor of the genitive is weak and because you have separated [them]. Yazīd ibn Quṭayb al-Sakūnī did read وجاعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر in the genitive, conjoined to the wording. Al-Akhfash said: حسبانا, that is, "by reckoning". He said: it is the plural of حساب, like شهاب and شهبان. Yaʿqūb said: حسبان is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of حسبت الشيء أحسبه حسبا وحسبانا, and الحساب is the noun. Others said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made the course of the sun and the moon by a reckoning that neither increases nor decreases, and by this Allah, Majestic and Mighty, pointed them to His power and His oneness. ذلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ: mubtadaʾ and khabar.

nahhas-irab:98-98.t:
Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĪsā, al-Aʿraj, Shayba and al-Nakhaʿī read فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ with a kasra on the qāf.
Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ with a fatḥa on the qāf. [Translator's note: the first reading intended is فمستقِرّ; the printed vowelling shows the fatḥa in both places.] In both it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), except that the implied form for those who put a kasra on the qāf is "so of them is one settled", while the fatḥa means "so they have a place of settlement". ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: they have a place of settlement in the womb and a place of deposit in the earth; this interpretation points to the fatḥa. Al-Ḥasan said: a place of settlement in the grave. Most of the exegetes say: المستقرّ is what is in the womb and المستودع is what is in the loins.

nahhas-irab:99-99.t:
وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً: the original form of ماء is «ماه»; the hāʾ is faint and so is the alif, so the hāʾ was replaced by a hamza, because the hamza is firm. فَأَخْرَجْنا بِهِ نَباتَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ, that is, everything that grows.
فَأَخْرَجْنا مِنْهُ خَضِراً: al-Akhfash said: that is, green (أخضر), as the Arabs say: «أرنيها نمرة أركها مطرة» ("Show it to me spotted [i.e. a cloud], and I will show it to you rainy"). وَمِنَ النَّخْلِ مِنْ طَلْعِها قِنْوانٌ دانِيَةٌ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Al-Farrāʾ permitted outside the Qur'an «قنوانا دانية», conjoined to what precedes it. Sībawayh said: among the Arabs are those who say قنوان.
Al-Farrāʾ said: this is the dialect of Qays; the people of the Ḥijāz say قنوان and Tamīm say قنيان; then they agree on the singular, saying قنو and قنو. [Translator's note: the vowel differences between these forms (e.g. قِنوان / قُنوان, قِنو / قُنو) are not marked in the source.] وَجَنَّاتٍ مِنْ أَعْنابٍ: the reading of the majority is with the accusative, conjoined, that is, "and We brought forth gardens". Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā and al-Aʿmash read — and it is the sound transmission of the reading of ʿĀṣim — وجنات in the nominative. Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim rejected this reading, so much so that Abū Ḥātim said: it is impossible, because the gardens are not of date-palms. Abū Jaʿfar said: the reading is permissible, and the interpretation is not along these lines; rather it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, that is, "and they have gardens", just as a group of readers read وَحُورٌ عِينٌ [al-Wāqiʿa: 22]. Sībawayh, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted the like of this, and there are many examples of it; on this basis too is وحورا عينا», which Sībawayh reported, and he recited: [al-Basīṭ] 135-
جئني بمثل بني بدر لقومهم ... أو مثل أسرة منظور بن سيّار
(Bring me the like of Banū Badr for their people, or the like of the family of Manẓūr ibn Sayyār.)
As for وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالرُّمَّانَ, only the accusative is possible in it, because of consensus on that. انْظُرُوا إِلى ثَمَرِهِ إِذا أَثْمَرَ: the reading of Abū ʿAmr and the people of Medina, the plural of ثمرة; the reading of Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī is إِلى ثَمَرِهِ with two ḍammas, the plural of ثمار; it has also been said: this is fruit-bearing wealth. It is transmitted from al-Aʿmash إِلى ثَمَرِهِ with a ḍamma on the thāʾ and a sukūn on the mīm, the ḍamma having been dropped because of its heaviness. [Translator's note: the variants intended are ثُمُرِه and ثُمْرِه; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading.] It may also be the plural of ثمر, like بدنة and بدن. Muḥammad ibn al-Samayfaʿ al-Yamānī read ويانعه, that is, "and its ripening"; Ibn Muḥayṣin and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read وينعه with a ḍamma on the yāʾ. Al-Farrāʾ said: the ḍamma is the dialect of some of the people of Najd.

nahhas-irab:100-100.t: وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ الْجِنَّ: «الجنّ» is the first object and شُرَكاءَ the second object, the implied form being "and they made the jinn partners for Allah". الجن may also be a badal (substitute) for شركاء, with the second object being لله. Al-Kisāʾī permitted the nominative of الجنّ in the sense of "they are the jinn". Ibn Masʿūd read وهو خلقهم, and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read وَخَلَقَهُمْ with a sukūn on the lām [Translator's note: i.e. وخَلْقَهم; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading]. He said: that is, "and they made [as partners] what they create", because they used to fashion a thing and then worship it.

nahhas-irab:101-101.t:
بَدِيعُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ, in the sense of "He is the Originator". Al-Kisāʾī permitted its genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and its accusative in the sense of بديعا السموات والأرض. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is wrong according to the Basrans, because it refers to what is past. أَنَّى يَكُونُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ صاحِبَةٌ: the noun of «تكن»; that is, from where could He have a child?
The child of anything is its likeness, and He has no likeness.

nahhas-irab:102-102.t: ذلِكُمُ: in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ: as a badal (substitute). خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ربكم may also be the khabar and «خالق» a second khabar, or [it may be] on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted the accusative in it.

nahhas-irab:104-104.t: قَدْ جاءَكُمْ بَصائِرُ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ, that is, signs and proofs by which one gains insight and reasons. بصائر has a hamza so that two quiescent letters do not meet, and the alif cannot take a vowel. فَمَنْ أَبْصَرَ فَلِنَفْسِهِ, that is, whoever reasons and comes to know. وَمَنْ عَمِيَ, and so did not reason, becoming like the blind. وَما أَنَا عَلَيْكُمْ بِحَفِيظٍ, that is, I have not been commanded to guard you from destroying yourselves.

nahhas-irab:105-105.t:
وَكَذلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ الْآياتِ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, that is, "and We vary the signs in the same way as what We have recited to you". وَلِيَقُولُوا دَرَسْتَ: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned the readings concerning it. Shuʿba transmitted from Abū Isḥāq from al-Tamīmī from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَلِيَقُولُوا دَرَسْتَ — he said: "you have read and learned". In the passage there is an ellipsis, that is, "and so that they say 'you have studied', We varied them". Abū Isḥāq said: this is as you say "So-and-so wrote this letter to his own death", that is, his affair ended in this; likewise, when the signs were varied, their affair ended in their saying "you have studied and learned". Abū Jaʿfar said: there is another good view on the meaning, namely that the meaning of نُصَرِّفُ الْآياتِ is "We bring them sign after sign, so that they say: 'you have gone over [them] with us'", and so they recall the first by the last; this is literal, while what Abū Isḥāq said is figurative. As for whoever reads دَرَسْتَ [Translator's note: the reading intended here is presumably دَرَسَتْ, "they have become effaced", as the explanation shows; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading], the best that has been said about it is that the meaning is "and so that they do not say: they have ceased and been effaced, and Muḥammad ﷺ brings nothing other than them". The best that has been said about دارست is that its meaning is "you have studied with us", so that its meaning is like that of درست. It has also been said: its meaning is "you have studied with the People of the Book"; this too is figurative, as he said: [al-Mutaqārib] 136-
فللموت ما تلد الوالده
(For death is whatever the mother bears.)

nahhas-irab:108-108.t:
وَلا تَسُبُّوا: a prohibition; the nūn is dropped from it because of the jussive. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade the believers to revile their idols, because He knew that if they reviled them the unbelievers would be repelled and increase in unbelief. Its parallel is His saying, Mighty and Majestic:
فَقُولا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّناً [Ṭā Hā: 44]. فَيَسُبُّوا: the answer to the prohibition, with the fāʾ. عَدْواً بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ: a maṣdar (verbal noun) and a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). It is transmitted from the people of Mecca that they read عدوا [Translator's note: i.e. عَدُوًّا, "enemies"]; this is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is a singular standing for a plural, like فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي إِلَّا رَبَّ الْعالَمِينَ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 77]. It is also transmitted from them عدوا with a ḍamma on the ʿayn and the dāl and a doubled wāw [i.e. عُدُوًّا]; this is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ and Qatāda.

nahhas-irab:109-109.t:
Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ لَئِنْ جاءَتْهُمْ آيَةٌ لَيُؤْمِنُنَّ with the light nūn. [Translator's note: i.e. ليؤمنَنْ; the printed vowelling shows the heavy nūn.] Sībawayh said: al-Khalīl said: وَما يُشْعِرُكُمْ, then he affirmed and said: (إنّا) [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably إنّها is meant]. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the reading of Mujāhid, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr. The people of Medina, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read أَنَّها with a fatḥa on the hamza. Al-Khalīl said: «أنها» is in the sense of «لعلها» ("perhaps it"). Abū Jaʿfar said:
On this reading too the complete stop is at وَما يُشْعِرُكُمْ; then he began and said (أنّها), and it carries the sense of affirmation. This is found in the speech of the Arabs: لعل and عسى come with the meaning of what will be. As for the view of al-Kisāʾī
that «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), this is wrong according to the Basrans, because it is made redundant only where it causes no ambiguity. Ḥamza alone read لا تؤمنوا with the tāʾ. [Translator's note: so in the source; the reading of Ḥamza is لا تؤمنون.]

nahhas-irab:110-110.t: وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصارَهُمْ كَما لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهِ «أول مرة»: this is a difficult verse, especially since it contains وَنَذَرُهُمْ فِي طُغْيانِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ. The meaning is: and We will turn their hearts and their eyes on the Day of Resurrection over the flame of the Fire, just as they did not believe in this world; and We leave them in this world, that is, We give them respite and do not punish them. So part of the verse concerns the Hereafter and part of it this world. Its parallel is وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ خاشِعَةٌ [al-Ghāshiya: 2], which is in the Hereafter, and عامِلَةٌ ناصِبَةٌ [al-Ghāshiya: 3], which is in this world.

nahhas-irab:111-111.t:
أَنَّنا: in the position of the nominative. وَحَشَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلًا ]: Hārūn the reader said:
that is, "face to face". Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: قبلا may mean "direction", as you say: لي قبل فلان مال ("I have money due from so-and-so"). [Translator's note: this first reading is قِبَلًا, which the printed vowelling does not show.] And (قبلا) with a ḍamma on the qāf and the bāʾ: there are three views on it. Al-Farrāʾ's position is that it means "guarantors", as He said أَوْ تَأْتِيَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْمَلائِكَةِ قَبِيلًا [al-Isrāʾ: 92]. The view of al-Akhfash is that it is in the sense of قبيل ("group by group"). On both views it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: وَحَشَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلًا, that is, "facing"; from this is إِنْ كانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِنْ قُبُلٍ [Yūsuf: 26], and from it are a man's قبل and دبر, for what is in front of him and behind him, and from it قبل الحيض ("the onset of menstruation"). Al-Ḥasan read وَحَشَرْنا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلًا, dropping the ḍamma from the bāʾ because of its heaviness. [Translator's note: i.e. قُبْلًا; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading.] ما كانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ: «أن» is in the position of the accusative as an exception not of the same kind as the first.

nahhas-irab:112-112.t:
وَكَذلِكَ جَعَلْنا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا: Sībawayh reported (جعل) in the sense of "describe". عَدُوًّا: the first object. لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ: in the position of the second object. شَياطِينَ الْإِنْسِ وَالْجِنِّ: it substitutes for (yadullu ʿalā) عدوّ; and you may make «شياطين» the first object and «عدوّا» the second object. The meaning of شيطان is one who is rebellious in disobedience to Allah the Exalted, whose harm reaches others; whoever is like this is a shayṭān, whether of mankind or of the jinn. Its meaning is "stretching far in evil", derived from الشطن, which is the rope. What the devils of the jinn whisper to the devils of mankind is called وحي ("inspiration") because it takes place only in secret. Their deceptive embellishment was called زخرف because they adorn it. وغُرُوراً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the meaning of يُوحِي بَعْضُهُمْ إِلى بَعْضٍ is "they deceive them by that with deception"; it may also be in the position of a ḥāl. [Translator's note: so in the source; the first characterisation presumably meant a maṣdar (absolute object), as the explanation "deceive … with deception" indicates.] Ibn ʿAbbās transmitted, with an isnad, that he said concerning His words يُوحِي بَعْضُهُمْ إِلى بَعْضٍ: Iblīs has a devil with every jinn and a devil with every human; one meets the other and says to him: "I have led my companion astray, so lead your companion astray in the same way", and the other says the like to him. This is their inspiring one another. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is indicated by وَإِنَّ الشَّياطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلى أَوْلِيائِهِمْ لِيُجادِلُوكُمْ [al-Anʿām: 121], and this clarifies its meaning.
فَذَرْهُمْ: an imperative carrying the sense of threat. Sībawayh said: one does not say وذر or ودع [in the past tense]; they dispensed with them by using ترك.
Abū Isḥāq said: the wāw is heavy, so since ترك, which has no wāw, has the meaning of what has the wāw, what has the wāw was abandoned. This is the meaning of his words, not their exact wording.

nahhas-irab:113-113.t: وَلِتَصْغى إِلَيْهِ: the lām of purpose (lām kay), and likewise وَلِيَرْضَوْهُ وَلِيَقْتَرِفُوا, except that al-Ḥasan read وَلِيَرْضَوْهُ وَلِيَقْتَرِفُوا with a sukūn on the lām, making it a lām of command carrying the sense of threat, as one says "do what you will". [Translator's note: i.e. ولْيرضوه ولْيقترفوا; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading.]

nahhas-irab:114-114.t:
أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ: accusative governed by أبتغي. حَكَماً: accusative as specification (bayān), or if you wish as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْكِتابَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise وَالَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ مُنَزَّلٌ مِنْ رَبِّكَ بِالْحَقِّ. فَلا تَكُونَنَّ: a prohibition emphasised with the heavy nūn; it takes a fatḥa because two quiescent letters meet, and it has also been said: because they are two things, one joined to the other.

nahhas-irab:115-115.t: وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ صِدْقاً وَعَدْلًا: a maṣdar (verbal noun) and a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:116-116.t: وَإِنْ تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ, that is, the unbelievers. يُضِلُّوكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ, that is, from the path that leads to the reward of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَخْرُصُونَ: [إن] in the sense of «ما» (negation).

nahhas-irab:117-117.t: (من) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), like لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ [al-Kahf: 12].

nahhas-irab:118-118.t: فَكُلُوا مِمَّا ذُكِرَ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ: [اسم is] the noun of the verb whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). According to the philologists, ذكر is with the tongue, and it is with the heart figuratively.

nahhas-irab:119-119.t:
وَما لَكُمْ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). أَلَّا: in the position of the accusative, the meaning being "and what is there for you in not eating of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned?". Sībawayh permits «أن» to be in the position of the genitive with an implied preposition. إِلَّا مَا اضْطُرِرْتُمْ إِلَيْهِ: in the position of the accusative as an exception. وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً: the noun of «إن»; it is acceptable for its noun to be indefinite because it conveys information and the predicate is not definite.
This is good according to Sībawayh, and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 137-
وإنّ شفاء عبرة لو سفحتها ... فهل عند رسم دارس من معوّل
(A tear, if I shed it, would be a cure; but is there any recourse at an effaced trace of an abode?)

nahhas-irab:121-121.t:
وَلا تَأْكُلُوا: a prohibition. مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ: the rāʾ takes a kasra because two quiescent letters meet.
وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٌ: the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».

nahhas-irab:122-122.t: Al-Musayyabī transmitted from Nāfiʿ ibn Abī Nuʿaym أَوَمَنْ كانَ مَيْتاً فَأَحْيَيْناهُ with a sukūn on the wāw. [Translator's note: i.e. أَوْ مَن; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading.] Abū Jaʿfar said: it may be construed according to the meaning, that is, "look and consider: shall I seek a judge other than Allah, or one who was dead and We gave him life?". Whoever gives the wāw a fatḥa makes it a conjunctive wāw preceded by the interrogative alif.

nahhas-irab:123-123.t: The lām of purpose (lām kay); it has been said that it is figurative, as He said: فَالْتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَناً [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8].

nahhas-irab:125-125.t: فَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلامِ, that is, He widens it as a reward [leading] to obedience to Him; it is a condition and requital (sharṭ wa-mujāzāh). وَمَنْ يُرِدْ أَنْ يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقاً حَرَجاً is like it. Ibn Kathīr read ضَيِّقاً with a light yāʾ [i.e. ضَيْقًا], as one says ليّن and لين, هيّن and هين. حرج is the active participle, and حرج is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description, as one says رجل عدل and رضى. [Translator's note: the two forms, حَرِج and حَرَج, are not vowelled in the source.] It has also been said: حرج is the plural of حرجة; its meaning is extreme narrowness, and from it comes "so-and-so is scrupulous (يتحرّج)", that is, he constrains himself in abandoning his desire for sins. كَأَنَّما يَصَّعَّدُ فِي السَّماءِ: we have already discussed it. كَذلِكَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, and likewise what has come before in His words «وكذلك جعلنا في كلّ قرية».

nahhas-irab:126-126.t: وَهذا صِراطُ رَبِّكَ مُسْتَقِيماً قَدْ فَصَّلْنَا الْآياتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَذَّكَّرُونَ (126) وَهذا صِراطُ رَبِّكَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). مُسْتَقِيماً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:127-127.t: لَهُمْ دارُ السَّلامِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise وَهُوَ وَلِيُّهُمْ بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ.

nahhas-irab:128-128.t: وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ: accusative governed by the omitted verb, that is, "and on the day He gathers them We will say". جَمِيعاً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). يا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ: a vocative in construct (munādā muḍāf). قَدِ اسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ وَقالَ أَوْلِياؤُهُمْ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ رَبَّنَا اسْتَمْتَعَ بَعْضُنا بِبَعْضٍ: the clearest thing said about it is that the jinn's enjoyment of mankind is that they took pleasure in mankind's obedience to them, and mankind took pleasure in accepting from the jinn, to the point that they committed fornication and drank wine. It has also been said: the jinn are the ones who enjoyed mankind, because mankind accepted from them. The first is preferable, because each of the two has enjoyed the other. The implied form in Arabic is: استمتع بعضنا ببعضنا. قالَ النَّارُ مَثْواكُمْ: mubtadaʾ and khabar. خالِدِينَ فِيها: accusative as a ḥāl. إِلَّا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ: an exception not of the same kind as the first. إِنَّ رَبَّكَ حَكِيمٌ, that is, in their punishment and in all His acts. عَلِيمٌ of the measure of their requital.

nahhas-irab:130-130.t:
The best that has been said about it is that the meaning of منكم is "[of you] in creation, legal responsibility and being addressed". قُصُّونَ [Translator's note: so in the source; يَقُصُّونَ is meant]
is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of رسل.

nahhas-irab:131-131.t: ذلِكَ: in the position of the nominative according to Sībawayh, in the sense of "the matter is that", because your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly. Al-Farrāʾ permitted it to be in the position of the accusative in the sense of "He did that".

nahhas-irab:133-133.t: كَما أَنْشَأَكُمْ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, in the sense of "and He makes whom He wills succeed after you, a succession like the way He produced you". مِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ قَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ: Zayd ibn Thābit read ذُرِّيَّةِ قَوْمٍ with a kasra on the dhāl and a doubled rāʾ and yāʾ [i.e. ذِرِّيّة], and Abān ibn ʿUthmān read ذريّة with a fatḥa on the dhāl, a light rāʾ and a doubled yāʾ [i.e. ذَرِيّة].

nahhas-irab:134-134.t: (ما) is the noun of (إنّ), the khabar (predicate) is لآت, and the lām is for emphasis.

nahhas-irab:135-135.t: قُلْ يا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلى مَكانَتِكُمْ إِنِّي عامِلٌ, that is, according to what I am upon. مَنْ تَكُونُ لَهُ عاقِبَةُ الدَّارِ: the noun of تكون. «من يكون» is also permissible, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) and its feminine gender is not real, like the feminine of the group. Al-Aʿraj read يا معشر الجنّ والإنس ألم تأتكم on the feminine of the group. مَنْ تَكُونُ لَهُ عاقِبَةُ الدَّارِ is in the position of the nominative, because what precedes an interrogative does not govern it; it may also be in the sense of الذي (relative noun), in which case it is in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:136-136.t: فَقالُوا هذا لِلَّهِ بِزَعْمِهِمْ: this is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz. The dialect of Banū Asad is بِزَعْمِهِمْ [Translator's note: i.e. بِزُعمهم, with ḍamma; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading], and so Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and al-Kisāʾī read it. The dialect of Tamīm and Qays, according to what al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī reported, is «بزعمهم» with a kasra on the zāy, even though Abū Ḥātim rejected the kasra; al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ did report it. فَما كانَ لِشُرَكائِهِمْ فَلا يَصِلُ إِلَى اللَّهِ: they were called partners because they assigned them a share of their wealth and said: they are our partners in it. ساءَ ما يَحْكُمُونَ: al-Kisāʾī said: (ما) is in the position of the nominative, that is, "evil is the thing they do". Abū Isḥāq said: «ما» is in the position of the nominative, and the meaning is "evil is the judgement they make".

nahhas-irab:137-137.t:
وَكَذلِكَ زَيَّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلادِهِمْ شُرَكاؤُهُمْ: this is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, the people of Kufa and the people of Basra, except Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and al-Ḥasan, who read وَكَذلِكَ زَيَّنَ with a ḍamma on the zāy, لِكَثِيرٍ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلادِهِمْ with قتل in the nominative and أولادهم in the genitive,
and شُرَكاؤُهُمْ in the nominative. Abū ʿUbayd reported that Ibn ʿĀmir and the people of Syria read وَكَذلِكَ زَيَّنَ with a ḍamma on the zāy, (لكثير من المشركين قتل أولادهم) with قتل in the nominative, أولادهم in the accusative, and شركائهم in the genitive. Someone other than Abū ʿUbayd reported from the people of Syria that they read وَكَذلِكَ زَيَّنَ with a ḍamma on the zāy, لِكَثِيرٍ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلادِهِمْ with قتل in the nominative and أولادهم in the genitive, and شركائهم in the genitive as well. [Translator's note: in these variants the printed vowelling repeats the main reading; the differences are as described in words.] Abū Jaʿfar said: these are four readings. The first is the clearest and soundest: «قتلا» is accusative governed by زيّن, «أولادهم» is genitive by the construct (iḍāfa), and شُرَكاؤُهُمْ is nominative governed by زيّن, not by القتل, because they adorned it and did not kill; they are their partners in religion and their chiefs. The second reading is that «قتل» is the noun of the verb whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), and «شركاؤهم» is nominative by an implied verb, because زيّن indicates it, that is, "their partners adorned it". On this basis ضرب زيد عمرو is permissible, meaning "ʿAmr struck him"; Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 138-
ليبك يزيد ضارع لخصومة
(Let Yazīd be wept for — by one humbled in a dispute.)
And Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of Ibn ʿAbbās, read يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ فِيها بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصالِ رِجالٌ [al-Nūr: 36] [Translator's note: the reading intended is يُسَبَّحُ in the passive; the printed vowelling shows the active], and Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAbla read قُتِلَ أَصْحابُ الْأُخْدُودِ النَّارِ ذاتِ الْوَقُودِ [al-Burūj: 4–5] [Translator's note: the reading intended is النارُ in the nominative; the printed vowelling shows the genitive], in the sense of "the fire killed them". As for what Abū ʿUbayd reported from Ibn ʿĀmir and the people of Syria, it is not permissible in either prose or poetry. The grammarians permitted separating the muḍāf from the muḍāf ilayhi only in poetry, and only by an adverb (ẓarf), because it does not [really] separate; with nouns other than adverbs it is a solecism (laḥn). As for what someone other than Abū ʿUbayd reported, which is the fourth reading, it is permissible on the basis that شركاؤهم is a badal (substitute) for أولادهم, because they are their partners in lineage and inheritance. لِيُرْدُوهُمْ: the lām of purpose (lām kay). وَلِيَلْبِسُوا عَلَيْهِمْ دِينَهُمْ, that is, they command them to falsehood, so the truth becomes covered over; by this they confuse.

nahhas-irab:138-138.t: وَقالُوا هذِهِ أَنْعامٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). وَحَرْثٌ حِجْرٌ: conjoined to the khabar. Abān ibn ʿUthmān read وَحَرْثٌ حِجْرٌ with a ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and the jīm, and al-Ḥasan and Qatāda read وَحَرْثٌ حِجْرٌ ] with a ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and a sukūn on the jīm [Translator's note: i.e. حُجُر and حُجْر; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading]; these are dialect forms with the same meaning. It is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn al-Zubayr وحرث حرج, with the rāʾ before the jīm, and so it is in the codex of Ubayy. There are two views on it: one is that it is like جبذ and جذب [i.e. metathesis]; the other view, which is sounder, is that it is from الحرج, which is narrowness, so its meaning is "forbidden"; from it is "so-and-so is scrupulous (يتحرّج)", that is, he constrains himself from entering into what he suspects of being forbidden. افْتِراءً: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) and a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:139-139.t:
وَقالُوا ما فِي بُطُونِ هذِهِ الْأَنْعامِ خالِصَةٌ لِذُكُورِنا is read in four ways. The reading of the majority: وَقالُوا ما فِي بُطُونِ هذِهِ الْأَنْعامِ خالِصَةٌ, with خالصة nominative and feminine. Qatāda read خالِصَةٌ in the accusative. Ibn ʿAbbās read وَقالُوا ما فِي بُطُونِ هذِهِ الْأَنْعامِ خالِصَةٌ لِذُكُورِنا in the construct (iḍāfa). [Translator's note: i.e. خالصةً and خالصُهُ respectively; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading.] Al-Aʿmash read خالص لذكورنا without the hāʾ. The first reading is on the basis of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). On the feminine gender referring to ما there are three views. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash said: this is for intensiveness. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is feminine because الأنعام is feminine. Some consider this view wrong, because what is in their bellies is not of them, so it does not resemble تلتقطه بعض السيارة [Yūsuf: 10], since "some of the caravan" is a caravan; but this does not bind al-Farrāʾ, because he makes it feminine only because what is in their bellies is livestock just as they are livestock. The third view is the best: the feminine is according to the meaning of ما and the masculine according to its wording; the proof of this is that after it comes وَمُحَرَّمٌ عَلى أَزْواجِنا, according to the wording. So the implied form is: "and they said: the livestock that is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively…". The accusative is, according to al-Farrāʾ, by "cutting off" (qaṭʿ), and according to the Basrans a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what is in the first genitive [phrase]. It may not be a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in الذكور, as زيد قائما في الدار is permissible, because the governor is not flexible, although al-Akhfash permitted it in some of his books. The third reading is on the basis that خالِصَةٌ is a second mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «لذكورنا», and the clause is the khabar of «ما»; «خالصه» may also be a badal (substitute) for «ما». The fourth reading treats «ما» as masculine in its wording.
يَكُنْ [Translator's note: the source begins discussing وإن يكن ميتة without quoting it fully]: in the sense of "and if what is in their bellies is dead", and the feminine in the sense of "and if the foetuses are dead".
Abū Ḥātim said: "and if the living being is dead". Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: the preferred reading is يكن with the yāʾ, because after it comes فَهُمْ فِيهِ and He did not say فيها. And وإن يكن ميتة in the nominative is in the sense of "occurs" [i.e. complete kāna]. Al-Akhfash said: that is, "and if there is in their bellies a dead one".

nahhas-irab:140-140.t: سَفَهاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun) and a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

nahhas-irab:141-141.t:
وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَنْشَأَ جَنَّاتٍ: in the position of the accusative; the tāʾ takes a kasra because it is a sound plural.
مَعْرُوشاتٍ: a naʿt (adjective), that is, with walls around them; it has also been said: because some of their branches lie over others. وَالنَّخْلَ وَالزَّرْعَ: conjoined. مُخْتَلِفاً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq said: this is a difficult question of grammar, because it may be said: He produced them when their produce, which is their fruit, had not yet varied. There are two answers to this. One is that He produced them by His saying خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ [al-Anʿām: 102], and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He produced them with their produce varying. The other answer is that He produced them having foreordained that in them. Sībawayh made this clear with his saying:
مررت برجل معه صقر صائدا به غدا ("I passed a man with a falcon, hunting with it tomorrow"), as a ḥāl, just as you say ليدخلنّ الدار آكلين شاربين ("they shall enter the house eating and drinking"), that is, foreordaining that. وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالرُّمَّانَ: conjoined. مُتَشابِهاً وَغَيْرَ مُتَشابِهٍ: as a ḥāl. One says حصاد and حصاد, جداد and جدّاد, صرام and صرام. [Translator's note: the variant vowellings, e.g. حَصاد / حِصاد, are not marked in the source.] وَلا تُسْرِفُوا: a prohibition.
إِنَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ, that is, He does not praise them nor reward them.

nahhas-irab:142-142.t:
وَمِنَ الْأَنْعامِ حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشاً: conjoined, that is, "and He produced of the livestock beasts of burden and small ones". The scholars have three views on الأنعام. One is that الأنعام is camels specifically. It has also been said: النعم is camels alone, and when there are sheep and cattle with them, they are also أنعام. The third view is the soundest: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā said: «الأنعام» is every animal Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has made lawful; the soundness of this is indicated by His saying, Majestic and Mighty: أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ الْأَنْعامِ إِلَّا ما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ [al-Māʾida: 1]. We have already discussed الحمولة and الفرش; among the best that has been said about them is that الحمولة are those made subservient and tractable for carrying loads, and «الفرش» is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created of hides and wool, which is sat upon and spread out. وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُواتِ الشَّيْطانِ: the plural of خطوة.
Both ḍamma and fatḥa are permissible; Abū al-Sammāl read خُطُواتِ الشَّيْطانِ with a fatḥa on the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. خَطَوات; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading].

nahhas-irab:143-143.t:
ثَمانِيَةَ أَزْواجٍ: there are six views on its accusative. Al-Kisāʾī said: it is accusative by an implied أنشأ. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: it is accusative as a badal (substitute) for حمولة وفرش, or, if you wish, as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Akhfash ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: it may be accusative governed by كلوا, that is, "eat the meat of eight pairs". It may be accusative as a badal for «ما» according to its position, and it may be accusative in the sense of "eat what is permitted, eight pairs". مِنَ الضَّأْنِ اثْنَيْنِ: Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and ʿĪsā read مِنَ الضَّأْنِ with a fatḥa on the hamza [Translator's note: i.e. الضَّأَن; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading]. Abān ibn ʿUthmān read من الضأن اثنان ومن المعز اثنان, in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Abū ʿAmr, al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read ومن المعز with a fatḥa on the ʿayn, and in the text (ḥarf) of Ubayy it is ومن المعزى اثنين. Abū Jaʿfar said: most common in the speech of the Arabs are المعز and الضأن with a sukūn; this is indicated by their saying in the plural معيز, which is the plural of معز, as one says
عبد and عبيد. Imruʾ al-Qays said: [al-Wāfir] 139-
ويمنحها بنو شمج بن جرم ... معيزهم حنانك ذا الحنان
(And Banū Shamaj ibn Jarm grant it their goats — have mercy, O Possessor of mercy!)
Abū ʿUbayd also preferred ومن المعز with a sukūn on the ʿayn; he said: because of their consensus on الضأن. We have mentioned that الضَّأْنِ has been read [otherwise]. ماعز and معز are like تاجر and تجر. As for معز [with fatḥa], it is permissible because it contains one of the guttural letters, and likewise ضأن. قُلْ آلذَّكَرَيْنِ: accusative governed by حرّم. أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: conjoined to it, and likewise أَمَّا اشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَرْحامُ. You added a prolongation (madda) to the connecting alif and said آلذكرين in order to distinguish statement from question. Dropping the madda is permissible, because «أم» indicates the question, as he said: [al-Mutaqārib] 140-
تروح من الحيّ أم تبتكر
(Will you set out from the tribe in the evening, or early in the morning?)

nahhas-irab:145-145.t: قُلْ لا أَجِدُ فِي ما أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً عَلى طاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً أَوْ دَماً مَسْفُوحاً أَوْ لَحْمَ خِنزِيرٍ فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ أَوْ فِسْقاً أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ باغٍ وَلا عادٍ فَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (145) قُلْ لا أَجِدُ فِي ما أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً عَلى طاعِمٍ: Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī read يَطْعَمُهُ [Translator's note: the reading intended is يَطَّعِمُهُ, as the explanation shows; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading]; its original form is يطتعمه, and it was assimilated after the tāʾ was changed into ṭāʾ. يَطْعَمُهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ, that is, unless what is eaten is carrion. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: Nāfiʿ ibn Abī Nuʿaym said to me, explaining: "unless that is carrion". Ibn Kathīr, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read إلا أن تكون ميتة, the implied form on this basis being "unless the thing eaten (fem.) is carrion". Abū Jaʿfar Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read إلا أن تكون ميتة in the nominative. أَوْ دَماً in the accusative: some grammarians say it is a solecism (laḥn), because it conjoins an accusative to a nominative, and the conjoined (maʿṭūf) must follow what it is conjoined to. But the reading is permissible, and it is authentically transmitted from an imam [of reading], on the basis that أو دما is conjoined to أن, because «أن» is in the position of the accusative and is a noun, the implied form being "except the being of carrion". أَوْ دَماً مَسْفُوحاً: a naʿt (adjective). أَوْ لَحْمَ خِنزِيرٍ: conjoined, and likewise أَوْ فِسْقاً; فإنّه رجس is meant to come later in order. There is a difficulty in the verse. It is said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade every fanged beast of prey and every taloned bird, and these two are not in the verse. There are several views on this. Among them: they asked about a specific thing, so the answer came specific; this is the position of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him. It has also been said: whatever is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ is included in the verse, conjoined to what follows إلا; this is a good view, and there are many examples like it. There is a third, clear view on the verse, namely that whatever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade is carrion, so that on this view the verse includes these things.

nahhas-irab:146-146.t:
وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هادُوا حَرَّمْنا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ: al-Ḥasan read ظفر ] with a sukūn on the fāʾ, and Abū al-Sammāl read ظفر with a sukūn on the fāʾ and a kasra on the ẓāʾ. Abū Ḥātim rejected the kasra on the ẓāʾ — Abū Ḥātim rejected the kasra on the ẓāʾ with a sukūn on the fāʾ [Translator's note: the source repeats this phrase] — and he did not mention this reading. He said: one also says أظفور. Al-Farrāʾ reported in the plural أظافير, أظافرة, أظافر and أظفار. وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ وَالْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُما إِلَّا ما حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُما: (ما) is in the position of the accusative as an exception. ظُهُورُهُما: nominative governed by حملت. أَوِ الْحَوايا: in the position of the nominative, conjoined to الظهور. [Its singular:] حاوية, plural حوايا; and حاوياء, like نافقاء and نوافق, and ضاربة and ضوارب; an alif replaced the yāʾ, as one says صحارى. أَوْ مَا اخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ: (ما) is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to ما حملت. There are several views on this; this is the soundest, and it is the view of al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, and reasoning requires that a thing be conjoined to what immediately precedes it, unless its meaning would then be unsound or some evidence points to something else. ذلِكَ جَزَيْناهُمْ, that is, "the matter is that".
وَإِنَّا لَصادِقُونَ: the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; the original form is إنّنا.

nahhas-irab:147-147.t: فَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ: a condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَقُلْ رَبُّكُمْ ذُو رَحْمَةٍ واسِعَةٍ, that is, because He was forbearing with you and did not punish you in this world. The original form of «ذو» is ذوى; if it were pronounced according to the original form, one would say ذوى like عصا. It has come in the Qur'an according to the original form in ذَواتا أَفْنانٍ [al-Raḥmān: 48]. Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, informed of the unseen, of what they would say, and said:
