nahhas-irab:148-148.t: سَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما أَشْرَكْنا وَلا آباؤُنا: conjoined to the nūn and alif [of أشركنا]; this is good because you brought لا for emphasis, and it conveys the meaning of negation of them all. It has also been said: the meaning of His saying لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما أَشْرَكْنا وَلا آباؤُنا is: "if Allah had willed, He would have sent a messenger to our forefathers who would have forbidden them polytheism and the prohibiting of what He made lawful, and they would have desisted, and we would have followed them in that and become accustomed to it, and our natures would not have been averse to it". So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refuted them in this and said: هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ مِنْ عِلْمٍ فَتُخْرِجُوهُ لَنا, that is, "do you have any proof that this is so?". إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ in this saying, وَإِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا تَخْرُصُونَ, and so you make the weak among you imagine that you have an argument.

nahhas-irab:149-149.t: قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ الْحُجَّةُ الْبالِغَةُ, that is, the one that cuts off the excuse of the one argued against and removes doubt from whoever examines it.

nahhas-irab:150-150.t: قُلْ هَلُمَّ شُهَداءَكُمُ: the mīm takes a fatḥa because two quiescent letters meet, as you say ردّ يا هذا; neither a ḍamma nor a kasra on it is permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already discussed its meaning, except that in Kitāb al-ʿAyn by al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, [it is said] that its origin is «هل أؤمّ», that is, "shall I make for you?"; then they used it so often that the one being sought came to say it, just as the origin of «تعالى» is that the one who is higher says it to the one who is lower, and they used it so often that the one lower came to say تعالى to the one higher.

nahhas-irab:151-151.t:
قُلْ تَعالَوْا أَتْلُ: the answer to the imperative. ما حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ: (ما) is in the position of the accusative, governed by the verb. أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئاً: al-Farrāʾ prefers (لا) to be of prohibition, because after it comes وَلا تَقْتُلُوا.
Abū Jaʿfar said: «أن» may be in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for «ما», that is, "I will recite to you the prohibition of associating partners". It may be in the position of the accusative in the sense of "for fear that you associate partners", in which case what is recited to them is قُلْ لا أَجِدُ فِي ما أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً [al-Anʿām: 145] to the end of the verse. It may also be in the position of the nominative in the sense of "it is that you associate nothing with Him". وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ إِحْساناً: a maṣdar (verbal noun). وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلادَكُمْ مِنْ إِمْلاقٍ, that is, from fear of poverty. وَلا تَقْرَبُوا الْفَواحِشَ: accusative governed by the verb. ما ظَهَرَ مِنْها وَما بَطَنَ: a badal for it. ذلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ, that is, "the matter is that"; it may also be in the sense of "He has made clear to you [and] enjoined you with it". لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ: so that you may be in hope of that.

nahhas-irab:152-152.t:
وَلا تَقْرَبُوا مالَ الْيَتِيمِ:
all of it is prohibition, which is why the nūn is dropped from it. وَبِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ أَوْفُوا:
that is, when you make a covenant with Allah, Majestic and Mighty, about something, or swear an oath to a person, then fulfil it. ذلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ:
like the first; the tāʾ is assimilated into the dhāl because it is close to it, and it may be dropped because [the remainder] indicates it.

nahhas-irab:153-153.t:
وَأَنَّ هذا صِراطِي مُسْتَقِيماً: this is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. Its implied form according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is "and because this is My path", as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ [al-Jinn: 18]. Al-Farrāʾ holds that it is in the position of the genitive in the sense of «ذلكم وصّاكم به», and "He enjoined you that this is My path, straight". Al-Kisāʾī holds that it is in the position of the accusative with this meaning, except that when the bāʾ was omitted it became accusative. Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read وَأَنَّ هذا with a kasra on the hamza, and this begins a new sentence. Whoever reads وَأَنَّ هذا with the light form [Translator's note: i.e. وأَنْ; the printed vowelling shows the doubled form in all three cases], for him هذا is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the accusative is also permissible. The meaning of وأنّ هذا صراطي مستقيما is: whoever travels it does not deviate.
مُسْتَقِيماً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). فَاتَّبِعُوهُ وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا السُّبُلَ, that is, do not follow the various religions.
فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ: the answer to the prohibition. ذلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ: like the first.

nahhas-irab:154-154.t: ثُمَّ آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ: two objects. تَماماً: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) and a maṣdar (verbal noun). عَلَى الَّذِي: genitive by على. أَحْسَنَ: a past verb included in the ṣila (relative clause); this is the view of the Basrans. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted it to be a noun, a naʿt (adjective) of الذي, and permitted مررت بالذي أخيك; they qualify الذي with a definite noun and what is close to it. This is impossible according to the Basrans, because it qualifies the noun before it is complete; the meaning according to them is "upon the one who does good". Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted الذي to be in the sense of الذين, that is, "upon those who do good". A fourth view is reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd; he said: it is like your saying, when Zayd is mentioned, مررت بالذي ضرب, that is, "the one whom he struck"; so the meaning is "as a completion of the good that Allah did to Mūsā, of the message and other things". وَتَفْصِيلًا: conjoined, and likewise وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةً.

nahhas-irab:155-155.t:
وَهذا كِتابٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). مُبارَكٌ: a naʿt (adjective); outside the Qur'an مباركا is permissible,
as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:156-156.t: أَنْ تَقُولُوا: in the position of the accusative in the sense of "for fear that you say". Al-Farrāʾ said: that is, "and beware lest you say".

nahhas-irab:157-157.t: أَوْ تَقُولُوا: conjoined to it. فَقَدْ جاءَكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ: [masculine verb] because البينة and البيان are one and the same.

nahhas-irab:158-158.t:
يَوْمَ يَأْتِي بَعْضُ آياتِ رَبِّكَ: تأتي is also permissible, like فَالْتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8] or like تلتقطه بعض السيارة [Yūsuf: 10]. Ibn Sīrīn read لا تنفع نفسا إيمانها.
Abū Ḥātim said: this is a mistake by Ibn Sīrīn. Abū Jaʿfar said: in this there is a subtle point of grammar that Sībawayh mentioned, namely that الإيمان and النفس each include the other, so the feminine is permissible. Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 141-
مشين كما اهتزّت رماح تسفّهت ... أعاليها مرّ الرّياح النواسم
(They walked as spears sway whose tips are set swinging by the passing of gentle breezes.)
because المرّ and الرياح each include the other. There is another view on it: that الإيمان is made feminine because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), just as a feminine maṣdar is made masculine, as in فَمَنْ جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ [al-Baqara: 275], because موعظة is in the sense of الوعظ, and as he said: [al-Ṭawīl] 142-
فقد عذرتنا في صحابته العذر
(The excuse has excused us in his companionship.)
According to one of the views, he made العذر feminine because it is in the sense of المعذرة.

nahhas-irab:159-159.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ, that is, they believed in part and disbelieved in part; likewise whoever introduces an innovation has brought what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, did not command, and so has divided his religion. And فارقوا دينهم ("they abandoned their religion") means Islam; everyone who abandons it has abandoned the religion he ought to follow. لست منهم في شيء: thus He made binding his dissociation from them. إنما أمرهم إلى الله: as consolation for the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:160-160.t: مَنْ جاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is a condition; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثالِها, that is, "he will have ten good deeds like it". Sībawayh reported: عندي عشرة نسّابات, that is, "I have ten men who are genealogists". Al-Ḥasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and al-Aʿmash read فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثالِها [Translator's note: i.e. عَشْرٌ أمثالُها, with tanwīn; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading], its implied form being "he will have good deeds, ten, their likes", that is, he will have of recompense ten times what is due to him. It may also be that he has a like, and the like is multiplied so that it becomes ten. فَلا يُجْزى إِلَّا مِثْلَها: the predicate of the verb whose agent is not named. [Translator's note: so in the source; مثلها is the second object of the passive verb.]

nahhas-irab:161-161.t:
قُلْ إِنَّنِي هَدانِي رَبِّي إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ دِيناً: al-Akhfash said: it is accusative governed by هداني. Others said:
it is accusative in the sense of "He made known to me", like هو يدعه تركا. Abū Isḥāq said: it may be construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is "He guided me to a straight path", as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَيَهْدِيَكَ صِراطاً مُسْتَقِيماً [al-Fatḥ: 2]. قِيَماً: from نعمته [Translator's note: so in the source; the text appears corrupt here]; and قيّما was made weak [i.e. قِيَمًا] by assimilation to the preceding vowel. مِلَّةَ إِبْراهِيمَ: a badal (substitute). حَنِيفاً: Abū Isḥāq said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from إبراهيم. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: it is accusative by an implied "I mean" (aʿnī).

nahhas-irab:162-162.t:
قُلْ إِنَّ صَلاتِي: the noun of «إنّ». وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيايَ وَمَماتِي: conjoined to it. The people of Medina read وَمَحْيايَ with a sukūn on the yāʾ in continuous recitation [Translator's note: i.e. ومحيايْ; the printed vowelling shows the fatḥa]. None of the grammarians permitted this except Yūnus, because it combines two quiescent letters; Yūnus permitted it only because it is preceded by an alif, and the prolongation in the alif takes the place of a vowel. Yūnus also permitted اضربانْ زيدا. The grammarians forbade this only because it combines two quiescent letters without assimilation in the second. Whoever reads with the reading of the people of Medina and wishes to be safe from solecism pauses on «محياي», and so is not committing a solecism according to all the grammarians. Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿĪsā and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read وَمَحْيايَ وَمَماتِي ] with assimilation [Translator's note: i.e. ومحيَيَّ; the printed vowelling repeats the main reading]. This is a good form in Arabic: since the yāʾ alters what precedes it to a kasra, and a kasra is not possible on the alif, its alteration was made to be its change into a yāʾ, as the philologists recited: [al-Kāmil] 143-
سبقوا هويّ وأعنقوا لهواهم
(They went before my desire [i.e. died before me] and hastened on to their own desire.)
[Translator's note: the following passage appears to belong to a later verse (6:164, وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى), part of whose discussion is missing in the source.] … a khabar (predicate). Al-Akhfash said: one says وزر يوزر, and وزر يزر, and وزر يوزر وزرا; and إزرا is also permissible, as one says إسادة.

nahhas-irab:165-165.t: وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلائِفَ الْأَرْضِ: two objects. لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ: accusative by the lām of purpose (lām kay), and it stands in place of «أن». إِنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ الْعِقابِ: the noun of «إنّ» and its predicate, and likewise وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned more than this on it in «Umm al-Qurʾān» [al-Fātiḥa]. The meaning is: "Say: praise be to Allah". الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ: a naʿt (adjective). وَجَعَلَ الظُّلُماتِ وَالنُّورَ: in the sense of "created"; when جعل is in the sense of خلق it takes only one object. ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ: mubtadaʾ and khabar; some Arabs say الذون. The meaning is: then those who disbelieve set up for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, an equal and a partner, while He alone created these things.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ طِينٍ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). There are two views on its meaning. One: He is the One who created your origin, meaning Adam ﷺ. The other: the sperm-drop is something Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created from clay in reality, then transformed it until the human being came from it. ثُمَّ قَضى أَجَلًا: an object. وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى عِنْدَهُ: mubtadaʾ and khabar. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: قضى أجلا means the term of death, and أَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى عِنْدَهُ is the term of the Resurrection; so the meaning on this basis is: He fixed a term and informed you that you remain until death, but did not inform you of the term of the Resurrection. It has been said: قضى أجلا is what We made known — that there is no prophet after Muhammad ﷺ — and وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى is the matter of the Hereafter. And it has been said: قضى أجلا is what we know of the times of the new moons, the crops and what resembles them, and أجل مسمّى is the term of death: a person does not know when he will die. ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ: mubtadaʾ and khabar, i.e. you doubt that He is one God; and it has been said: you dispute about that.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: وَهُوَ اللَّهُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned it; among the best of what has been said about it is that the meaning is: "and He is Allah; He knows your secret and your open [speech] in the heavens and in the earth". وَيَعْلَمُ ما تَكْسِبُونَ: (ما) is in the position of an accusative [by] يعلم.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: (ما) is negation and not a condition; therefore the yāʾ remains in تأتيهم. Their turning away from them is their disbelief in them.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
(كم) is in the position of an accusative by أهلكنا; يروا does not govern it, for in an interrogative only what comes after it governs [it]. مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ ما لَمْ نُمَكِّنْ لَكُمْ: He did not say «لهم» because it comes by way of a shift of address.
وَأَرْسَلْنَا السَّماءَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِدْراراً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَجَعَلْنَا الْأَنْهارَ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ: two objects.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: One also says قرطاس [i.e. qurṭās as well as qirṭās; Translator's note: the vowelling that distinguishes the two forms is not shown in the source]. فَلَمَسُوهُ: conjoined; and the answer of لو is لَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: وَقالُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ: in the sense of هلّا (why not). وَلَوْ أَنْزَلْنا مَلَكاً لَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ: the noun of that whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ مَلَكاً لَجَعَلْناهُ رَجُلًا: i.e. if We had sent down to them an angel in its [true] form, they would not have seen it; and if We made it a man, what they confuse for themselves would have been confused for them as well, and they would have said: "This is a sorcerer like you". Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: they used to say to their weak ones: "Muhammad is only a human being; there is no difference between him and you", thereby confusing them and making them doubt; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that if He sent down an angel in the form of a man, they would find a way to confusion, as they do.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ: with a kasra or a ḍamma on the dāl because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the kasra is the original, and the ḍamma because after the quiescent letter there is a ḍamma. فَحاقَ بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ: i.e. its punishment.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
كَتَبَ عَلى نَفْسِهِ الرَّحْمَةَ: al-Farrāʾ said: if you wish, this is the end of the sentence, and then you begin anew with لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ; and if you wish, it is in the position of an accusative. الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ: al-Akhfash said:
if you wish, الَّذِينَ is in the position of an accusative as a badal (substitute) for the kāf and mīm. Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] claimed that this view is an error, because no badal is made for the one addressed, nor for the speaker: one does not say "I passed by you, Zayd" or "I passed by me, Zayd", because this is not ambiguous so as to need clarifying. It has been said: «الذين» is a singular vocative. And a third view has been stated, which is the best of them: الذين is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is فَهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيًّا: two objects. فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: a naʿt (adjective); al-Akhfash permitted the nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the accusative is permissible as praise; and al-Farrāʾ said:
[the accusative] by cutting off (ʿalā al-qaṭʿ). وَهُوَ يُطْعِمُ وَلا يُطْعَمُ: this is the reading of the majority; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid and al-Aʿmash read وَهُوَ يُطْعِمُ وَلا يُطْعَمُ. [Translator's note: the source prints the same vowelling for both; the variant is ولا يَطْعَم ("and does not eat").]

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: مَنْ يُصْرَفْ عَنْهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمَهُ: the reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr. The Kufans read مَنْ يُصْرَفْ with a fatḥa on the yāʾ [i.e. يَصرِف], and this is the choice of Abū Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd. On Sībawayh's view the preferred reading is «من يصرف» with a ḍamma on the yāʾ, because Sībawayh said: "The less implication there is, the better." If one reads من يصرف with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, its implied form is "whoever Allah turns the punishment away from"; and if one reads من يصرف [with a ḍamma], its implied form is "whoever the punishment is turned away from". وَذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْمُبِينُ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
قُلْ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْبَرُ شَهادَةً: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). شَهادَةً: as explanation (bayān) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)]; the meaning is "which thing of all things is greatest in testimony, that I may call it to witness against you?". قُلِ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ: mubtadaʾ and khabar. وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هذَا: the noun of that whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). الْقُرْآنُ: a naʿt (adjective) of it. لِأُنْذِرَكُمْ بِهِ: accusative by the lām of purpose (lām kay). وَمَنْ بَلَغَ: in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the kāf and mīm. There are two views on its meaning: one is "and [that I may] warn whomever the Qur'an reaches"; the other is "and whoever reaches puberty". By this He indicated that whoever has not reached puberty is not addressed [by the law] nor bound to worship. أَإِنَّكُمْ: with two hamzas according to the original form; if you lighten the second you say
أينّكم. Al-Aṣmaʿī reported from Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ أاإنكم; this is a known dialectal form, in which an alif is placed between the two hamzas out of dislike for their meeting. وَإِنَّنِي: according to the original form; وإني is permissible by omission. بَرِيءٌ: the khabar of «إن».

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
الَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ: in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). يَعْرِفُونَهُ: in the position of the khabar (predicate).
الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ: in the position of a nominative, a naʿt (adjective) of the first الذين; it may also be a mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is فَهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ.
i.e. their testing. It is read in five ways. Ḥamza [and] al-Kisāʾī read ثم لم يكن
with the yāʾ,
and فِتْنَتُهُمْ in the accusative. This is a clear reading, because أَنْ قالُوا is the noun of «يكن», and it is masculine in form, while «فتنتهم» is the khabar (predicate). The people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ with the tāʾ, and فِتْنَتُهُمْ in the accusative; he made «أن قالوا» feminine, according to Sībawayh, because «أن قالوا» is the fitna. Its parallel according to Sībawayh is the Arabs' saying ما جاءت حاجتك, and al-Ḥasan's reading تلتقطه بعض السيّارة [Yūsuf: 10]; and Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl metre] 130-
وتشرق بالقول الذي قد أذعته ... كما شرقت صدر القناة من الدّم
(And you choke on the word you have spread abroad, as the upper part of the spear-shaft is choked with blood.)
Others than Sībawayh said: he made «أن قالوا» in the sense of المقالة (the saying, feminine). ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read وما كان فتنتهم إلّا أن قالوا. Al-Aʿraj, Muslim ibn Jundab, Ibn Kathīr, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī, ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Ḥafṣ, al-Aʿmash in the transmission of al-Mufaḍḍal, al-Ḥasan, Qatāda and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read
ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ with the tāʾ and فِتْنَتُهُمْ in the nominative, as the noun of تكن, the khabar being إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا. These are four readings, and the fifth is ثم لم يكن with the yāʾ and (فتنتهم) in the nominative, treating الفتنة as masculine because it is in the sense of al-futūn; like it is فمن جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ [al-Baqara: 275].
وَاللَّهِ: genitive by the wāw of oath, which is a substitute for the bāʾ because of its closeness to it. رَبِّنا: a naʿt (adjective). Whoever reads it in the accusative takes it as a vocative, i.e. "O our Lord"; this is a good reading, because it carries the sense of submission and humble entreaty.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ: in the position of an accusative, i.e. "out of aversion (كراهة) that they understand it". وَفِي آذانِهِمْ وَقْراً: conjoined. One says وقرت أذنه ("his ear became deaf") with a fatḥa on the wāw; Abū Zayd reported from the Arabs أذن موقورة ("a deafened ear"), so on this basis [it is] وقرت with a ḍamma on the wāw [i.e. the passive وُقِرت]. The singular of الأساطير is اسطارة, and أسطورة is also said; it is also said to be the plural of أسطار, and أسطار is the plural of سطر — one says سطر and سطر [i.e. saṭr and saṭar].
